note: This guide supports transparent, phrase-based reflection. It is not a semantic judgement, grading rubric, or proof that an unrecognised idea was absent.

lessons.principle: Understand the customer's intended use

signals.label: intended use
signals.why: Knowing how the oil will be used helps narrow the options before discussing a premium product.
signals.question: What will the customer mainly use it for?

signals.label: budget and price range
phrases: how much they want to spend
signals.why: A suitable recommendation needs to fit the amount the customer is comfortable spending.
signals.question: Have you asked what price range feels comfortable?

signals.label: pack size or brand preference
signals.why: Pack size and a stated preference can matter as much as the product label.
signals.question: Would a different pack size or familiar brand suit them better?

lessons.principle: Understand the occasion and practical requirement

signals.label: the occasion
signals.why: The occasion helps clarify what the clothing needs to work for.
signals.question: What is the occasion, and when will they wear it?

signals.label: practical needs
signals.why: Practical needs make the options relevant rather than simply attractive.
signals.question: Is there a particular comfort, fit or use requirement?

signals.label: the customer's budget
signals.why: A clear budget helps you show suitable options without assumptions.
signals.question: What spending range have they set?

lessons.principle: Match the phone to everyday usage

signals.label: everyday phone use
signals.why: Understanding regular tasks helps separate useful features from specifications the customer may never use.
signals.question: Which tasks matter most in their normal day?

signals.label: essential features
signals.why: Specific feature priorities help compare verified models accurately.
signals.question: Which feature would make the biggest practical difference?

signals.label: budget and priorities
signals.why: The right comparison balances needs and budget, not just the biggest specification list.
signals.question: Which needs are essential, and what is their comfortable budget?

lessons.principle: Balance quantity, ripeness and timing

signals.label: how much the household can use
signals.why: Quantity is more useful when matched to how much the household can realistically consume.
signals.question: How much is likely to be used before the next purchase?

signals.label: ripeness and timing
signals.why: Timing matters because fruit at different stages of ripeness may be used on different days.
signals.question: Which fruit should be ready first, and which can ripen later?

signals.label: avoiding waste and fitting the budget
signals.why: Thinking about waste and spending together can help the customer buy a practical amount.
signals.question: What quantity balances the customer's budget with the risk of spoilage?

lessons.principle: Explain verified product differences

signals.label: a verified difference
signals.why: A specific, verified difference is more useful than a vague claim that one product is better.
signals.question: Which difference can you demonstrate or verify?

signals.label: why the difference matters to this customer
signals.why: A difference becomes meaningful when connected to how the customer plans to use the shirt.
signals.question: Which of those differences matters for their intended use?

signals.label: care or limitations
signals.why: Care instructions and limitations help customers make an informed comparison.
signals.question: Is there a care requirement they should know before deciding?

lessons.principle: Clarify and confirm the alteration

signals.label: the exact change requested
signals.why: A specific requested change reduces the risk of completing work the customer did not ask for.
signals.question: Which part should be changed, and by how much?

signals.label: how the customer wants it to fit
signals.why: The customer's preferred fit should be understood rather than guessed from a general request.
signals.question: Can you confirm the preferred fit with the garment or a fitting?

signals.label: agreement before work begins
signals.why: Confirming the work, price and realistic timing creates a shared expectation.
signals.question: Have you repeated the agreed work and timing back to them?

lessons.principle: Set realistic expectations for a salon service

signals.label: the customer's desired result
signals.why: Understanding the result the customer hopes for helps you discuss what is feasible.
signals.question: What part of the reference matters most to them?

signals.label: what is realistically possible
signals.why: Explaining relevant limits avoids promising an identical result when starting conditions differ.
signals.question: What may differ from the reference in this case?

signals.label: agreement before starting
signals.why: A clear discussion of the process, price and expected result lets the customer decide comfortably.
signals.question: Have you explained the process and got agreement before beginning?

lessons.principle: Verify measurements and compatibility

signals.label: measurements or exact dimensions
signals.why: A photo alone may not show the exact dimensions needed for a safe fit.
signals.question: Which measurement can you check before selecting the part?

signals.label: model or compatibility details
signals.why: Exact model and connector details can prevent an unsuitable recommendation.
signals.question: Can the customer provide the exact model or part details?

signals.label: safety and fit verification
signals.why: For repair parts, correct fit and safety matter more than making a quick sale.
signals.question: Does this need an in-person check or a qualified person's confirmation?

lessons.principle: Check the economics before discounting

signals.label: actual cost and margin
signals.why: Checking actual item economics helps avoid agreeing to a price that is not sustainable.
signals.question: Have you checked the current cost and room available on these items?

signals.label: the exact items and offer conditions
signals.why: A discount should be based on the specific items, quantity and any real offer conditions.
signals.question: Which items and quantities are included in the request?

signals.label: the relationship without automatic discounting
signals.why: You can value a regular customer without making an unchecked discount automatic.
signals.question: How can you explain your price respectfully if a discount is not workable?

lessons.principle: Compare the complete online and in-store offer

signals.label: the exact model or product
signals.why: A fair comparison starts by checking that both listings are for the same model and variant.
signals.question: Are both products exactly the same model and specification?

signals.label: total price and terms
signals.why: The headline price may not include the same items, service or terms.
signals.question: What is included in the final price and what terms apply?

signals.label: genuine local-shop value
signals.why: Explain only the support or convenience your shop genuinely provides.
signals.question: Which benefit can you actually provide and stand behind?

lessons.principle: Evaluate a bulk order before negotiating

signals.label: ingredient and packaging costs
signals.why: The full material and packaging cost matters when calculating whether the order is worthwhile.
signals.question: Have you counted all materials and packaging for this quantity?

signals.label: workload, time and capacity
signals.why: A large order can use capacity needed for other work, so time and workload belong in the calculation.
signals.question: Can the shop complete the order on time without disrupting other commitments?

signals.label: delivery and payment terms
signals.why: Clear timing and payment terms reduce avoidable disputes on a large order.
signals.question: What timing and payment arrangement would make the order workable?

lessons.principle: Keep bargaining respectful and sustainable

signals.label: a clear and consistent price
signals.why: A calm explanation of the genuine price is more useful than becoming defensive.
signals.question: Can you explain what the quoted price includes?

signals.label: the shop's viable limit
signals.why: Knowing the shop's actual limit helps avoid agreeing to an unsustainable price.
signals.question: Have you checked the lowest workable price rather than guessing?

signals.label: a respectful choice
signals.why: Respectful language keeps the conversation open even when the price does not change.
signals.question: How can you leave the decision with the customer respectfully?

lessons.principle: Respect the customer's pause

signals.label: respect for the decision
signals.why: Respecting the pause avoids turning a normal decision into a pressured sale.
signals.question: How can you make it clear that the customer can decide later?

signals.label: an optional question about uncertainty
signals.why: A gentle, optional question may reveal whether any information would help.
signals.question: Could you ask whether they want any detail clarified, without insisting?

signals.label: useful information for later
signals.why: A simple way to revisit the information can help without manufacturing urgency.
signals.question: What information could they take away to compare in their own time?

lessons.principle: Support a family discussion without pressure

signals.label: respect for the family discussion
signals.why: Acknowledging that the customer wants another opinion respects their decision process.
signals.question: How can you acknowledge the request without trying to override it?

signals.label: clear information to share
signals.why: Accurate details can help the customer explain the option to their family.
signals.question: What relevant details could they take away or share?

signals.label: an open invitation to return
signals.why: An easy, pressure-free return keeps the relationship open.
signals.question: How can you invite them back without implying the product will disappear?

lessons.principle: Verify product-specific storage information

signals.label: checking the exact product or batch
signals.why: Storage guidance can differ by product and batch, so the exact information matters.
signals.question: What label or batch information can you check?

signals.label: verified storage instructions
signals.why: The correct storage conditions should come from reliable product-specific guidance.
signals.question: Where can you verify the storage requirements for this product?

signals.label: avoiding an unsupported shelf-life promise
signals.why: Avoiding an unsupported guarantee protects the customer and the shop.
signals.question: How will you explain what is known without promising more than the label supports?

lessons.principle: Understand the customer's concern about a service

signals.label: the specific concern
signals.why: Finding out whether the concern is about process, time or cost makes the explanation more relevant.
signals.question: Which part are they unsure about?

signals.label: what the service includes and its limits
signals.why: Clear scope helps the customer understand what they are paying for.
signals.question: Have you explained what is and is not included?

signals.label: freedom to choose
signals.why: The customer should be able to decide whether the service is worthwhile for them.
signals.question: How can you leave the choice with them after explaining?

lessons.principle: Listen, establish facts and resolve fairly

signals.label: acknowledging and listening
signals.why: Acknowledging the concern helps the customer feel heard before facts are checked.
signals.question: Have you let them explain what happened without interruption?

signals.label: checking purchase and storage facts
signals.why: The timeline and storage details can help clarify what may have happened without assuming blame.
signals.question: What facts can you check with the customer?

signals.label: a fair next step within actual policy
signals.why: A resolution should follow the shop's real policy and the facts, not a promise made too early.
signals.question: What fair option is actually available under your policy?

lessons.principle: Take responsibility for a delayed alteration

signals.label: honest acknowledgement and update
signals.why: A direct, honest update recognises that the customer relied on the date you gave.
signals.question: Have you clearly explained what is and is not finished?

signals.label: a realistic alternative
signals.why: A practical alternative is more useful than a rushed promise that may fail again.
signals.question: What option can genuinely be completed before the occasion?

signals.label: a confirmed feasible timeline
signals.why: A revised deadline should reflect actual capacity, not an attempt to end the conversation.
signals.question: What timing can you honestly commit to?

lessons.principle: Investigate a compatibility complaint fairly

signals.label: the exact phone model
signals.why: Compatibility depends on the specific device, not only the brand name.
signals.question: Have you checked the customer's exact phone model?

signals.label: the accessory's specifications
signals.why: The accessory's exact model and supported specifications need to be compared with the phone.
signals.question: What product detail can confirm whether they are compatible?

signals.label: actual support or return terms
signals.why: The next step should follow the real terms that applied at purchase.
signals.question: Have you checked the bill and the actual support terms before promising a remedy?

lessons.principle: Clarify the gap between expectation and result

signals.label: the customer's specific concern
signals.why: A specific description helps identify what the customer feels is different.
signals.question: Have you asked which part of the result concerns them?

signals.label: what was agreed beforehand
signals.why: Comparing the original discussion with the customer's experience helps clarify the gap.
signals.question: What had both of you agreed before the service?

signals.label: a feasible next step
signals.why: Any adjustment should be realistic and within the service provider's capabilities.
signals.question: What can genuinely be adjusted, and what needs to be explained?

lessons.principle: Remember preferences but confirm today's need

signals.label: checking the current requirement
signals.why: A customer's needs can change, so today's request matters more than an old pattern.
signals.question: What is different about what they need today?

signals.label: using past preferences carefully
signals.why: Past preferences can help start a conversation, but they should not replace asking.
signals.question: How can you mention the usual choice while checking whether it still suits them?

signals.label: respecting privacy and choice
signals.why: Remembering should make service easier, not expose private purchase details or create assumptions.
signals.question: How can you use the information discreetly and let the customer choose?

lessons.principle: Set a respectful credit boundary

signals.label: checking the outstanding balance and terms
signals.why: Checking the actual balance and agreed terms avoids decisions based only on memory or pressure.
signals.question: Have you checked the exact pending amount and due date?

signals.label: a clear and consistent boundary
signals.why: A clear, consistent boundary protects the shop without humiliating the customer.
signals.question: How can you explain the boundary calmly and consistently?

signals.label: a practical way to settle or review
signals.why: A realistic next step can keep the conversation constructive without extending credit automatically.
signals.question: Can you agree on a practical way to review or settle the existing amount?

lessons.principle: Use contact details only for the agreed update

signals.label: the purpose the customer agreed to
signals.why: The customer agreed to a particular update, not every future message.
signals.question: What exactly did the customer ask to be notified about?

signals.label: the agreed contact method
signals.why: Using the agreed channel keeps the update relevant and expected.
signals.question: Which contact method did they agree to use?

signals.label: separate permission for promotions
signals.why: Permission for a service update is not permission for promotional messages.
signals.question: Have you asked separately before sending any marketing?

lessons.principle: Recommend only when it fits a current need

signals.label: checking the customer's current need
signals.why: A previous good experience does not automatically mean the customer needs another product today.
signals.question: What are they looking for now?

signals.label: a relevant and useful recommendation
signals.why: A recommendation should solve a current need rather than simply add another sale.
signals.question: How does the option connect to the need they have described?

signals.label: respecting the customer's choice
signals.why: Being comfortable with a customer declining helps preserve trust.
signals.question: How will you make it easy for them to say no?
